I will keep the same 6 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I have done this for many years, so I will not change too much. On my land, if I cut fertilizer too hard and the crop turns weak, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer money, so I will stay a bit on the safe side. I only have 6 mu and two people at home, and some family labor goes off-farm, so I will do things in a simple way that I can manage on time. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the phosphorus in at sowing, give enough nitrogen, and water about three times with my well if the season is normal. Wheat needs a steady stand, so I will do rotary tillage after maize and get the field level. For maize, I will still use hybrid seed because around here the hybrids yield better and stand better; I have seen that in nearby fields for years. After wheat harvest I will sow maize quickly, use a little base fertilizer and then topdress nitrogen later, with about two irrigations if rain is not enough. I will spray when I see the usual weeds, aphids, rust, or armyworm pressure, but I will not skip it if the field starts showing trouble. I am aiming for a solid harvest, not gambling on saving a few bags of input.
